subject: NectarAI — onboard phasing, safety margin, and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nectarai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@nectarai.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: rough sizing and timing questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Caleb and I pulled together some clarifying questions so we can compare internal forecasts against the numbers you shared:

- We expect a steady-state peak of ~220 concurrent inference threads for our chat product, with batch embedding jobs overnight (roughly 1.5M tokens/day).
- We want a firm minimum-guarantee for 30 days after go-live, and then a staged ramp.

Two asks: can you send a concise set of commitment options that map to cluster sizes, the minimum GPU floor, and typical warm-up timelines? Also curious about how Redwood defines the safety margin for early months (we may want a 20% headroom).

Appreciate a one-page summary we can share with finance + ops.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Operations | NectarAI
elena.ruiz@nectarai.com

[Attachment: internal-traffic-estimates.csv (csv)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nectarai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@nectarai.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: rough sizing and timing questions

Elena —

Thanks for the detail and the file. Attaching a compact offer that maps three commitment tiers to cluster footprints and ramp timelines. High level:

- Tier A (Conservative): 8x A100-equivalent GPUs minimum, supports baseline concurrency up to ~150 with modest tail latency. Ramp to 16 over 8 weeks.
- Tier B (Balanced): 16x GPUs minimum, target steady-state for your peak concurrency (~220) with 15–20% safety margin; ramp to 32 over 10–12 weeks.
- Tier C (Aggressive): 32x GPUs minimum, designed for headroom and bursty growth; staged ramp to 48 over 12 weeks plus planned warm-up credits.

Notes on safety margin: we typically size for 10–25% depending on traffic variability. For your overnight batches we recommend separate embedding lanes (2–4 GPUs) to avoid latency interference.

I've looped in Ben (SE) to add a quick technical appendix and Marissa on contracting/credits. I also included a proposed DocuSign link for the Balanced offer if you'd like to pilot.

Next steps: Ben will attach a brief matrix, and Marissa will propose invoice/credit cadence. If this looks reasonable we can lock an initial 60-day pilot window with a 30-day minimum floor.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

[Attachment: Redwood_Offer_NectarAI_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nectarai.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@nectarai.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity: rough sizing and timing questions

Elena — quick technical note from the SE side.

Based on the traffic profile and 1.5M tokens/day:
- Recommendation: Balanced (Tier B) as Sean outlined. 16x A100-equivalent GPUs in the primary cluster, plus a 3-GPU embedding lane.
- Warm-up plan: pre-seed KV cache across the primary shards for 72 hours prior to go-live using synthetic traffic; expected warmup cost: ~8 hours of full load per shard.
- Safety margin logic: we set concurrency headroom at 20% for the first 60 days, then re-evaluate with telemetry. If you want to cap spend, we can set auto-burst constraints to limit cross-tier spillover.

Attachments: I exported a simple sizing worksheet that maps concurrency to GPU usage (see GPU_Onboard_Timeline.xlsx).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

[Attachment: GPU_Onboard_Timeline.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nectarai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@nectarai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: rough sizing and timing questions

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying items from finance/ops after a quick review:

1) Minimum floor: finance is insistent on a defined 30-day minimum at the start of production. For the Balanced tier they want that expressed as a fixed dollar amount and GPU count (we proposed 16 GPUs).
2) Ramp triggers: ops asked that ramp steps be tied to usage thresholds (e.g., 80% sustained for 14 days) rather than fixed calendar weeks — can Redwood support usage-triggered scaling within the reserved model?
3) Credits: will you confirm how warm-up credits apply and when they are invoiced?

If we can see a short clause on ramp triggers and an invoice example, we can route to legal and finance.

—Elena

On a related note, would you be open to a 2-month pilot with a 30-day hard floor at a slightly reduced rate to de-risk ramp? Caleb and I think that could speed approval.

Elena

[Quoted message omitted]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nectarai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Caleb Turner <caleb.turner@nectarai.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: rough sizing and timing questions

Elena —

Great questions. Short answers below and proposed next steps so finance/legal can proceed:

- Minimum floor: confirm 16 GPUs as the 30-day hard floor for the Balanced tier. We'll include an invoice example in the final SOW showing pro-rated billing for the minimum period plus applied warm-up credits.
- Usage-triggered ramping: yes — we can implement rule-based ramp triggers (e.g., 80% sustained concurrency over 14 days) that initiate pre-agreed increases. Those ramps will still count toward the committed capacity for billing; if you prefer, we can add a soft-approval window so your ops team provides a confirmation before the charge is applied.
- Warm-up credits: Redwood provides 72 hours of warm-up credits valid during the initial 30-day window; credits are applied as a line-item credit on the first invoice after go-live.

Pilot option: happy to offer a 60-day pilot (two months) with a 30-day hard floor at 90% of the listed Balanced rate (as an introductory credit). Marissa will follow up with the exact SOW language and a DocuSign link.

Action items:
- Marissa to send SOW + invoice example (by EOD Tue).
- Ben to share final sizing worksheet with ops-runbook notes.
- Elena/Caleb to confirm pilot start date (we suggested 2027-06-01) or propose alternatives.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
